exercise.name: Hip Raise (bent knee)

reference.title: Hip Raise (bent knee)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip flexion, then posterior pelvic tilt and lumbar flexion, knees bent)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the knees come up, breathe out as the hips curl off the mat, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 0.9 s knees up, 1 s hips up, short pause, 1.7 s down, 1.2 s feet down

prescription.tempo: About 1 s up, brief pause, 2-3 s down; no swinging
prescription.progression: Slower lowering, then the straight-leg lying leg hip raise.

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms by your sides palms down, knees bent with the feet flat on the mat.
Lift the feet and bring the thighs to vertical, knees bent about 90 degrees.
Breathe out and curl the hips off the mat, drawing the knees toward the chest.
Roll the pelvis down slowly, then lower the feet until they just touch the mat.
Brief touch, low back heavy, then go again.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the knees to roll the hips up
mistakes.fix: Pause at vertical and curl the pelvis with the abdominals.

mistakes.mistake: Opening the knee angle as the hips lift
mistakes.fix: Hold the knees at about 90 degrees all the way.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the feet onto the floor
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and only tap the mat.
Keep the head and shoulders relaxed on the mat.

kinematics.norm: From feet on the floor to thighs vertical, then past vertical as the pelvis curls (clinical opinion)
Knees travel toward the chest at the top (clinical opinion)
The pelvis curls until the tailbone clears the mat; this curl brings in the lower abdominals (Clark 2003)
Shoulders and head stay on the mat (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5062, Hip Raise (bent knee), video (movement reference)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)
Sarti et al. 1996, muscle activity in upper and lower rectus abdominis during abdominal exercises (Arch Phys Med Rehabil 77(12):1293-1297; PMID 8976314)
Clark, Holt and Sinyard 2003, electromyographic comparison of the upper and lower rectus abdominis during abdominal exercises (J Strength Cond Res 17(3):475-483; PMID 12930172)
Axler and McGill 1997, low-back loads over a variety of abdominal exercises: searching for the safest abdominal challenge (Med Sci Sports Exerc 29(6):804-811)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.

Low-back pain, disc problems or flexion intolerance: start with a posterior pelvic tilt or the dead bug; partial curl-ups gave the best abdominal challenge for the least spine compression in one model study (Axler and McGill 1997).
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before trunk-flexion work.
modify: Low-back discomfort: smaller curl (tailbone just off the mat).
Neck tension: relax the head on the mat.
regressions: Posterior pelvic tilt with feet on the floor.
progressions: Lying leg hip raise on the floor.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the pelvis toward the ribs; reverse-crunch style curls raised lower rectus activity (Sarti 1996, Clark 2003).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lift the thighs from the floor to vertical (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Lift the thighs from the floor to vertical (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help curl the pelvis and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help curl the pelvis and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Press the arms into the mat to steady the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Press the arms into the mat to steady the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keep the elbows straight as the hands press down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keep the elbows straight as the hands press down (clinical opinion).
